setting: Mio's home while reading an uncle's letter; imagined overseas places use soft vignette edges so they are not mistaken for present reality

sentences.english: One day, a letter arrived from my uncle, who lives in a far country.
sentences.japanese: ある日、遠い国に住む叔父さんから手紙が届きました。

sentences.english: When I opened the envelope, there were beautiful stamps and a story about his new life.
sentences.japanese: 封筒を開けると、きれいな切手と、新しい生活の様子が書かれていました。

sentences.english: My uncle is working abroad, and every day, he is learning something new in a foreign culture.
sentences.japanese: 叔父さんは海外で働いていて、毎日、異国の文化の中で新しいことを学んでいるそうです。

sentences.english: In the letter, there were also photos of an old square and some stone buildings.
sentences.japanese: 手紙には、古い広場や石造りの建物の写真も入っていました。

sentences.english: “The world is wide, and each country has its own culture and tradition,” my uncle wrote.
sentences.japanese: 「世界は広くて、どの国にも、その国ならではの文化や伝統があるんだよ」と叔父さんは書いていました。

sentences.english: Looking at the photos, my sister said with shining eyes, “Someday I want to take a flight and go to a far island.”
sentences.japanese: 写真を見ながら、妹は目を輝かせて「いつか飛行機に乗って、遠い島へ行ってみたい」と言いました。

sentences.english: My uncle will come back to Japan soon.
sentences.japanese: 叔父さんはもうすぐ日本に帰ってくるそうです。

sentences.english: He wrote, “Please come to the airport to meet me.”
sentences.japanese: 「空港まで迎えに来てね」と書いてありました。

sentences.english: My sister and I are waiting for that day.
sentences.japanese: 妹とわたしは、その日を心待ちにしています。

sentences.english: Travel is a time to meet not only new scenes, but also new feelings in ourselves.
sentences.japanese: 旅は、新しい景色に出会うだけでなく、自分の中の新しい気持ちにも出会える時間なのかもしれません。
